main_body: A dark grey rune stone slab (rows 6-31) with a lighter grey rounded cap at rows 7-10 and a darker body below carrying cyan rune glyphs
top_band: grey #5c5a64 rows 7-10 (4 rows), sits directly under the outline at row 6 and is only slightly lighter than the body (L=92 vs 69), no wider than the shaft
evidence: The column scan at x=8 shows an outline at row 6, a lighter cap at rows 7-10 (L=92), a dark line at row 11, then the body at L=69 down to row 31. The cap is only about 23 L lighter than the shaft, which is under the 25 L threshold for a top. Its silhouette is a flat rounded band no wider than the shaft, so it reads as the red 'flat band cap' of the guide rather than an ellipse top face. The cap is a flat band over a dark underside and the shaft is a flat front face with glyphs painted on it, so this is a front elevation and it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. All of its dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), so the outline is a near-black sticker line, while the references have tinted outlines (1% and 33% neutral). The body is a large flat fill of one dark grey with no grain or stone texture. Only the cyan runes add variation. It is much thinner and flatter than the references.
